first.rationale: Onboarding completion is down 4% and activation is also declining, so simplifying onboarding addresses the clearest current funnel constraint while leveraging prior evidence of improved time-to-value and SMB activation. Use a standard experiment with guardrails on qualified pipeline, product-qualified activation, retention signals, and downstream revenue to ensure higher completion does not reduce lead quality or long-term value. Promotional pricing may counter competitor pressure, but it carries greater risk of attracting low-value accounts and does not directly address the onboarding and activation deterioration.

final.rationale: Run a limited onboarding-shortening experiment because completion is down 4% and the verified record shows a strong improvement in completion, time-to-value, and 30-day retention. Guard against the signup-simplification downside observed in SMBs: monitor qualified revenue, activation quality, conversion to meaningful product use, and 30-day retention, with stop conditions if downstream value deteriorates. This directly addresses the current onboarding constraint without using pricing to acquire potentially lower-quality accounts.
